name: number-field
title: Number field
summary: Lets people enter a number as a number — typed in their locale's form or stepped by a key or a button, kept within limits, with its unit beside it — as a field of a form that looks and measures like a text field.

anatomy.description: The Field: the label row with its glyph and its requirement mark, and the supporting row with the help and the error text. In a look whose input floats the label it draws no label row.
The number input, as the Field's one control: the box, the number in it, the prefix and the suffix, the two steppers, and the label that floats in the box in the looks that float one.

props.name: label
props.note: Names the number input. In a filled or outlined look the input draws it, floating in its box, and the Field draws no label row (FLD-25, NMI-8).

props.name: labelHidden
props.note: Hides the label wherever it would be drawn: the Field's row, or the input's floating label (FLD-25). Where no message is shown either, the bare number input, named by its own label, is that control without a frame.

props.name: error
props.note: The Field puts its number input in the input's own error condition (FLD-8, NMI-10); the steppers stay as they are.

props.name: disabled
props.note: The Field disables its number input, and with it both steppers (FLD-14, NMI-32); the number field is then left out of its form (NUM-48).

props.name: required
props.note: The Field exposes its number input as required (FLD-10, NMI-12).

props.name: invalidText
props.note: Shown by the Field, in its supporting row (FLD-28).

behavior.text: THE number field SHALL be a Field that frames one number input, and nothing else. It SHALL give label, labelHidden, supportingText, errorText, error, disabled, required, optional, requiredMark, requiredText and optionalText to its Field and every other prop to its number input, each unchanged; SHALL hold the label-icon slot for its Field; and SHALL emit its number input's events as its own, each once. THE number field SHALL be as wide as the place it stands in, and its number input SHALL fill it: it is a block with no width of its own, as its Field is (FLD-1), around a control that fills the width it is given (NMI-36). It SHALL draw no part of its own, hold no state of its own and have no token of its own: what it shows, how it behaves and what it exposes to assistive technology SHALL be exactly what that Field and that number input do when a product places the one in the other (FLD-1 to FLD-28; NMI-1 to NMI-46) — the label row and its requirement mark (FLD-2 to FLD-6), or the label that floats in the box with the Field's row left out (FLD-25, NMI-7, NMI-8); the supporting row and the error (FLD-7 to FLD-9, FLD-26); the name, the description and the states (FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14, NMI-12, NMI-32); a text that is not a number shown as an error in the Field's row, in the input's words (FLD-28, NMI-21); and the two steppers, which are the number input's Buttons and stand inside its box (NMI-25).
behavior.verify: The twin test: every fixture of the number field has a twin, the Field's fixture number-<id>, a Field around a number input written by hand with the same values; on every platform that draws both, the two are the same picture and the same accessibility tree. A difference is a finding in a member or in the exchange between them (NMI-45), never a baseline to update.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has forms (the web) THE number field SHALL be the one control the form sees: it SHALL take name, submit its number input's value as that input submits it — a decimal number with ASCII digits and a period, or an empty string WHILE it holds none (NMI-35) — reset to the value it was first given, restore it on navigation, report to the form's constraint validation exactly what its number input would report there (a missing value WHILE required is true and it holds none, NMI-12; a bad input WHILE an entry error lasts, NMI-21), and be left out WHILE disabled is true or a disabled group of the form holds it; its number input and its Field SHALL take no part in the form themselves. WHEN the action key asks for the form's submission (NMI-20) the form asked SHALL be the number field's own.
behavior.verify: Unit, on the web: a form with one number field of value 12.5 shown in de-DE submits one entry, "12.5", under the field's name; reset and restore reach the number input; required true with no value reports valueMissing on the number field, and "12 apples" committed reports badInput, each focusing its number input when the form reports it; Enter in the input presses the form's default button (BTN-30).

behavior.text: WHEN the number field is given focus — by the product, by a press on any part of it that FLD-12 or NMI-14 gives to the input, or by a form that reports its validity — THE number field SHALL pass the focus to its number input and SHALL add no stop to the focus order: it has one stop, its input, and the steppers are none (NMI-25). A press on a stepper SHALL step and move no focus, in the number field as in the bare input (NMI-26). WHILE focus is inside it THE number field SHALL count as focused for its Field (FLD-13).

IF the number field is placed in a Field THE number field SHALL in debug builds report that it is a field already and that the bare control is the number input, and both SHALL still render (FLD-15). WHILE it stands in a field group THE number field SHALL follow that group's disabled, through its own Field, and take nothing else from the group (FGR-14).

THE number field SHALL have no words of its own and SHALL read none: requiredText and optionalText are read by its Field (FLD-24), incrementLabel and decrementLabel by its number input (NMI-44), each from the instance's prop and then from the product's words.

keyboard.action: The number input's (its accessibility block; NMI-20, NMI-23). The number field handles no key and adds no focus stop (NUM-49).

accessibility.labeling: The number field adds nothing to what its members expose and coordinates nothing: the Field gives the number input its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled states (FLD-8, FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14), and the number input carries them on its own element with its value, its limits and its value text (NMI-12, NMI-34). Assistive technology meets one spin button named by label and two buttons that are no focus stops, exactly as it meets a Field around a number input written by hand.
notes: One level down is the same thing: a Field with a number input in it. Every fixture has that pair as its twin, and the accessibility tree of the two is the same (NUM-47).
On the web the two members stand in the number field's own shadow root, so the form meets the number field and not the input (NUM-48); focus passes through to the input (NUM-49).
Two levels down, for a number whose label is elsewhere and that shows no message, is the number input alone, named by its own label: beside a slider under one row title, in a table, in a toolbar.

web.name: tanrei-number-field
web.notes: The tag is `tanrei-number-field`, the class `TanreiNumberField`, the React name `NumberField`. Members: `<tanrei-field>` holding one `<tanrei-number-input>` in its default slot; the product places none. The host is `display: block`, as the Field is, so a number field is as wide as its place and its input fills it (NUM-47, NMI-36). Value member: `tanrei-number-input`. The host is the form's element — `name`, the value and its state as the input gives them (the decimal string, or nothing while disabled), validity anchored on the input (`valueMissing`, `badInput`), reset to the `value` attribute, restore, `form`, a disabled fieldset — and the input inside has no `name`. The `value` property is `number | null` and the attribute a decimal string, declared as the member declares them. Props, set as properties on the member each is from. On the Field: `label`, `labelHidden`, `supportingText`, `errorText`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `requiredMark`, `requiredText`, `optionalText`. On the number input: `variant`, `size`, `value`, `placeholder`, `readOnly`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `noSteppers` (the inverse of `steppers`, attribute `no-steppers`), `incrementLabel`, `decrementLabel`, `prefixText`, `suffixText`, `valueText`, `align`, `minFractionDigits`, `maxFractionDigits`, `locale`, `invalidText`. Attributes are the members' own: kebab-case, except `readonly`, `min`, `max` and `step`. Props of one name on both members — `label`, `labelHidden`, `error`, `disabled` — are the Field's; the input's are never set by the element and reach the input through the connection. Events: `input`, `change`, `action` and `entryerror` are the number input's own composed events and leave by themselves, with the host as their target and `value` already new at `change`; `action` stays cancelable. None is stopped and none is copied; a stepper's own `click` is the Button's and is not an event of the spec. Slots: `label-icon` is passed to the Field by a slot element of the same name, rendered only while the host has a child for it. The element has no other slot: the steppers are the input's own Buttons, not the product's children. Parts: the member hosts are `field` and `number-input`. Exported from the Field: `label`, `label-icon`, `requirement-label`, `supporting-text`. Exported from the number input: `container`, `outline`, `active-indicator`, `label`, `requirement-label`, `input`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `stepper`. Two names collide, `label` and `requirement-label`. Each is exported with its member's name before it, always (`field-label`, `number-input-label`, `field-requirement-label`, `number-input-requirement-label`), and under the bare name from both members as well, because the two are one thing to a person and are never drawn at once: FLD-25 is the sentence that holds it. `stepper` is a part of a member's small part: the number input exports the two Buttons' hosts under that name, and nothing of the Button's inside is exported. Focus: the shadow root does not delegate. `focus()` and `blur()` call the number input's; a press on the label row focuses the input by FLD-12, a press on the box by NMI-14, a press on a stepper steps and moves no focus (NMI-26), and a press on the help does nothing. The connection is the Field's with its control (FLD-25, FLD-26, FLD-28; NMI-45); the element takes no part in it. Parts and tokens of its own: none. The element writes no custom property: `--tanrei-comp-field-*`, `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, `--tanrei-comp-number-input-*` and, for the steppers, `--tanrei-comp-button-*` reach the members by inheritance, and one number field is set apart by setting any of them on the element. What its twin cannot do that it does: nothing. The twin: `<tanrei-field label="Quantity" supporting-text="Up to 99 per order." required><tanrei-number-input name="quantity" min="1" max="99" increment-label="Increase" decrement-label="Decrease"></tanrei-number-input></tanrei-field>`. Words: none of its own (NUM-51).

swiftui.name: TanreiNumberField
swiftui.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the number input as a view of its own, and this as the Field around it. Its name, its props and its idiom: `TanreiNumberField("Quantity", value: $quantity, in: 1...99, step: 1)`, shaped as the platform's own pair, `TextField(_:value:format:)` and `Stepper(value:in:step:)`: `value` is a `Binding<Double?>` (and an overload for `Binding<Int?>`, which sets `maxFractionDigits` to 0), written on every commit, which is the change event; `min` and `max` are one optional `ClosedRange` or partial range. Built on `TextField` with `.keyboardType(.decimalPad)` (`.numbersAndPunctuation` where a minus sign is needed) and a `FormatStyle` from `locale`. `labelHidden` follows `.labelsHidden()`, `disabled` follows `.disabled(_:)`, `action` is `onSubmit:`. The field carries `.accessibilityAdjustableAction` for increment and decrement and `.accessibilityValue` with the value text; the steppers are `TanreiButton`s with `.focusable(false)`. The drawing is Tanrei's on every Apple platform; `Stepper` itself is not used to draw. The product's words are read from the `\.tanreiWords` environment value.

compose.name: TanreiNumberField
compose.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the number input as a view of its own, and this as the Field around it. Its name, its props and its idiom: Compose idiom, as `TextField`: `TanreiNumberField(value: Double?, onValueChange: (Double?) -> Unit, label = "Quantity", min = 1.0, max = 99.0)`; the caller keeps `value` (state hoisting) and `onValueChange` is called on a commit, `onInput` while typing. `enabled` is the inverse flag and `isError`, `readOnly`, `prefix` and `suffix` keep Compose's names. Built on `BasicTextField` with `KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Decimal)` (`Number` while `maxFractionDigits` is 0) and `java.text.DecimalFormat` for `locale`. Semantics: `Role` has no spin button, so the field sets `stateDescription` (the value text), `ProgressBarRangeInfo` for the limits and `setProgress`, plus custom accessibility actions for increase and decrease; the steppers are `TanreiButton`s with `Modifier.focusProperties { canFocus = false }`. A held stepper repeats from `pointerInput` with the component's own timings. The product's words are read from `LocalTanreiWords`.

flutter.name: TanreiNumberField
flutter.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the number input as a view of its own, and this as the Field around it. Its name, its props and its idiom: Flutter idiom, as `TextField` and `InputDecoration`: `TanreiNumberField(value: 12, onChanged: (num? v) {…}, labelText: 'Quantity', min: 1, max: 99)`, with `hintText`, `helperText`, `errorText`, `prefixText`, `suffixText` and `enabled` keeping `InputDecoration`'s names, `enabled` the inverse flag. `TanreiNumberFormField` wraps it as a `FormField<num?>` (`validator`, `onSaved`, `autovalidateMode`). Built on `TextField` with `TextInputType.numberWithOptions(decimal:, signed:)` and no input formatter that refuses characters (NMI-16); formatting and parsing use `NumberFormat` from the `intl` package with `locale`. `Semantics(value:, increasedValue:, decreasedValue:, onIncrease:, onDecrease:)` makes it adjustable; the steppers are `TanreiButton`s with `canRequestFocus: false`. Tabular figures are `FontFeature.tabularFigures()`. The product's words are read from the `TanreiWords` inherited widget, which the app fills from its own localizations.

react-native.name: NumberField
react-native.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the number input as a view of its own, and this as the Field around it. Its name, its props and its idiom: React Native idiom, as `TextInput`: `<NumberField label="Quantity" value={quantity} onValueChange={setQuantity} min={1} max={99} />` with `value: number | null`. Built on `TextInput` with `inputMode="decimal"` (`"numeric"` while `maxFractionDigits` is 0; `keyboardType="numbers-and-punctuation"` on iOS where a minus sign is needed, because its decimal pad has none). `accessibilityRole="adjustable"`, `accessibilityValue={{ min, max, now, text }}` and `accessibilityActions` increment and decrement with `onAccessibilityAction`; the steppers are `Button`s with `focusable={false}`. Formatting uses `Intl.NumberFormat` where the engine has it (Hermes does) and falls back to ASCII digits with the locale's separator. `fontVariant: ['tabular-nums']`. Follows the app's direction where an ancestor's is not known. The product's words are read from the `TanreiWordsProvider` context.
